analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. docs/developer/test.md gains a 'Provider authorization guidance' section (patch hunk 17-28) describing ProviderAuthorizationReadinessTests. The supplied head_text units (lines 476-1401) show unchanged surrounding test guidance. docs/provider/attestation.md bumps the date and adds a paragraph at head lines 141-142. The paragraph tells the operator to keep existing MDM profiles installed and wait for a fresh coordinator decision when status/doctor reports that App Attest authorizes the connection but removal readiness is stale. It notes that a displayed serving lease can remain valid after removal readiness goes stale. It refers to ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.swift (`summary`).

This is consistent with the existing TB-011/T-053/T-057 posture: removal guidance requires a coordinator decision received within 10 seconds, a current daemon snapshot and unexpired authorization, and a local state-file rewrite cannot extend readiness. The new text is fail-safe because it tells operators not to remove profiles prematurely, which reduces the T-057 stranding risk. It does not weaken serving authorization, grant any trust, or touch secrets, keys or the encrypted cache path. Nothing in the diff changes code, so no attack surface, authorization, attestation, encryption or billing behavior changes.

Limits: the Swift source (ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.swift) and the tests are not in the supplied batch, so the accuracy of the documented behavior (separate lease versus removal-readiness decisions, 10-second window, receipt-window boundary) was not verified against code. The attestation.md patch excerpt is truncated, but the changed-range map is complete. No security-relevant regression is identified. The threat model needs no update beyond possibly noting the lease/readiness separation, which already appears covered by T-053/T-057.
